meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (national unified jurisdiction; incorporation administered through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones One-Stop-Shop)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified, Napoleonic-influenced; Islamic Sharia is a principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution; commercial matters governed by Civil Code No. 131/1948 and Commercial Code No. 17/1999)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United States Trade and Investment Framework Agreement (1999)
Egypt-United Kingdom Investment and Trade Continuity Agreement (2020)
Egypt-United Arab Emirates Bilateral Investment Treaty (2001)
Arab League Investment Agreement and Arab Investment Court regime
Double Tax Agreements: Egypt-USA (1981, effective 1982), Egypt-UK (1980, as amended), Egypt-France (1982), Egypt-Germany (1987, as amended), Egypt-UAE and Egypt-Saudi Arabia DTAAs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering as amended by Law No. 181 of 2008 and Law No. 36 of 2017; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 1223 of 2013, as amended; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended (including beneficial-ownership register obligations implemented through GAFI registration instructions); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; Anti-Terrorism Law No. 94 of 2015; FATF 40 Recommendations as applied through the Middle East and North Africa Financial Action Task Force (MENAFATF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each foreign incorporator's passport and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention); documents must be authenticated by the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate in the issuing country and subsequently reviewed by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Cairo

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and banker's due-diligence certificate confirming source of funds and account conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in the incorporator's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egyptian Embassy/Consulate legalization, then review by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly notarized power of attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation agent or law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership chain chart (UBO structure) of any corporate shareholder holding 25% or more of the LLC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the corporate shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The incorporators, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories must be screened at onboarding and continuously thereafter (at minimum annually) against: (i) the Egyptian Consolidated Terrorist List administered by the Central Bank of Egypt and the Public Prosecution; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List under Resolutions 1267/1989/1988 and 1373; (iii) OFAC-SDN and EU sanctions lists as a best-practice precondition of the target payment rails (Stripe and Apple IAP) and international correspondent banking; and (iv) domestic and international PEP indicators requiring enhanced due diligence under FATF Recommendations 12 and 22 and the Egyptian AML Executive Regulations. Screening must include source-of-wealth verification, adverse-media assessment, and re-screening triggered by any amendment to the UBO schedule; failure to file a complete UBO schedule with GAFI blocks issuance of the commercial registration certificate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI One-Stop-Shop electronic portal and e-incorporation module (Saham): https://www.gafi.gov.eg and https://services.gafi.gov.eg; in-person filing remains available at the GAFI Commercial Registration Department
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal name must be in Arabic script and must include the limited-liability company suffix and its accepted abbreviation where applicable; the Latin-script English transliteration may be registered as a parallel commercial name but cannot serve as the sole legal name. Names must not consist of abbreviations alone, must avoid confusing similarity with existing registered names, must not begin with numeric characters or symbols, and must reflect the lawful business purpose consistent with ISIC 6201 software and information services.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Misr / Egypt / Egyptian (requires prior ministerial license)
Bank / Insurance / Financial (without a financial services license)
Islamic / Christian / Holy or other exclusively religious references
Arab as a leading token (requires exceptional clearance)
International / Universal / Global (requires demonstrated multi-jurisdiction activity)
Names of the President, ministers, or state honorifics
Suez Canal / Electricity / Gas / Petroleum or other utility and concession terms
Words contrary to public order, decency, or public morality
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written grievance to the GAFI Commercial Registration Department (One-Stop-Shop) within 15 business days, attaching the rejection notice, the proposed corrected name, and evidence of non-confusion with existing registrations. GAFI must issue a decision within 30 days. Adverse decisions may be escalated to the GAFI Vice-Chairman's Grievance Committee; final administrative review lies with the State Council's Administrative Justice Court, which must be petitioned within 60 days of the final refusal. Re-filing a new name reservation with a fresh fee remains available without prejudice at any stage.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permitted for the primary commercial registration: GAFI requires a tangible registered office in Egypt evidenced by a lease agreement with a term of at least one year, proof of physical occupancy, and building consent/signage. Serviced offices within GAFI-licensed incubators or co-working centers are acceptable only where the operator issues a formal occupancy certificate and permits unannounced GAFI and tax authority inspections.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 10-15% probability of an unannounced GAFI or municipal inspection within the first 12 months of operation for a low-risk software entity; the probability declines to approximately 5-8% annually thereafter, but rises to 25% or higher if the registered address is in a residential zone, if sanctions/AML flags arise, or if third-party complaints are received.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 148 of 2019, Articles 98-129 (Limited Liability Companies); Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 51 of 2020; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 regarding GAFI one-stop shop registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registry and One-Stop Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association for a Limited Liability Company, in Arabic, authenticated before the competent Notary Public and filed through the GAFI Investor Gateway
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs. Founders freely put the share capital in the memorandum; cash contributions must be deposited in a bank account in Egypt before filing. No escrow account requirement. Non-resident founders may hold 100% ownership and contribute in foreign currency through licensed banks.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: By written resolution of the board of directors of the Company, dated 2 April 2025 and unanimously adopted, it is resolved: (1) the GAFI incorporation certificate issued for the Company is ratified; (2) the subscription of 1,000 ordinary shares, representing the full capital declared in the memorandum, is approved; (3) the registered office is fixed at Unit 9, Third Floor, Cairo Technology Park, New Cairo, Egypt; (4) Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary are appointed as officers with authority defined in the governance charter; (5) the said officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute GAFI filings, and complete commercial registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI corporate name reservation and investor account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop through Investor Gateway online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an investor account on GAFI Investor Gateway, submit three Arabic company name alternatives including an English transliteration, pay the name reservation fee electronically, and obtain a name reservation certificate. The name must end with Limited Liability Company or its Arabic equivalent and must not conflict with registered marks or corporate names.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each founder and resident manager
Three proposed company names with Arabic and English transliterations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on similarity grounds, submit alternate names within 7 operating days or appeal the rejection to the GAFI Registry Appeals Committee with evidence of prior use.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Authentication of memorandum and articles of association before notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public desk co-located at GAFI Investor Center in Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct an Egyptian advocate to draft the Arabic Memorandum and Articles of Association under Law No. 148 of 2019. Every founder signs all counterparts, and the Notary Public authenticates capacity and signature pages, affixing stamp duty and official seals.
required_dossiers: Draft memorandum of association in four counterparts
Draft articles of association in two counterparts
Bank confirmation of cash capital deposit or signed capital undertaking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary questions signature authenticity or legal capacity, convene the parties at the notary office, re-execute defective pages, and resubmit for the same authentication session.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of incorporation file to GAFI Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registry and One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarised formation file on the Investor Gateway, pay the GAFI statutory fees in EGP through the official e-finance channel, and await legal review of the statutory content, registered office declaration, capital subscription and permissible ISIC code. The case reference will be tracked digitally.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate confirming deposit of the cash portion of capital
Registered office acceptance undertaking by premises owner
Nomination and acceptance letters of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to GAFI requests for clarification through the portal within 15 working days; if the case is suspended, submit an administrative objection to the GAFI Dispute Resolution Committee under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of GAFI incorporation certificate and company national identifier
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After statutory clearance, GAFI records the LLC in the electronic companies registry and issues the official electronic Incorporation Certificate showing the company name, national identification number, registered office, capital and incorporation date.
required_dossiers: Proof of full payment of filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of any certificate data discrepancy by filing a GAFI rectification form with notarised supporting documents; correction is completed within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial register entry and municipal business operation license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office of the Ministry of Trade and Industry and the local district (Hayy/City Council)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the commercial register extract using the GAFI certificate and articles, then apply to the local district for a business activity license covering professional information technology services. The district verifies zoning, building code compliance and classification of the ISIC 6201 activity.
required_dossiers: Legalized lease contract of the registered office
Civil Defense preliminary fire safety inspection report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commercial registry detects data inconsistencies, file a notarised correction statement; if the district refuses the municipal license, request a reconsideration hearing and cure zoning or civil defense observations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, VAT certificate and e-invoicing activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) local tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the tax registration form with the local tax authority to obtain the corporate Tax Card. Voluntarily or mandatorily register for VAT when taxable software services exceed EGP 500,000 or in preparation for Stripe and Apple IAP sales. Request activation of the e-invoicing and e-receipt system code.
required_dossiers: Bank account certificate and ownership structure disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ETA withholds registration or requests additional KYC evidence, submit supplemental documentation to the tax office case handler and, if needed, file a complaint with the ETA Internal Solutions Center under the Unified Tax Procedures Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil defense fire safety clearance and environmental screening attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil Defense Authority of the Ministry of Interior and Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) screening group
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange physical inspection of the office by Civil Defense and obtain the fire safety certificate for commercial occupancy. Submit a self-declared environmental category 'D' exemption statement to the EEAA/GAFI environmental window because the software tracking activity has no industrial discharge, effluent or VOC emission.
required_dossiers: Office floor plan and legal lease
Fire extinguisher and evacuation compliance declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inspection flags missing extinguishers or blocked exit routes, remedy the defects, pay the administrative re-inspection fee and re-inspect within 10 working days; environmental classification objections are reviewed by EEAA's Environmental Inspection Unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social insurance and labor office registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) local branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the employer registration Form NOSI 1, submit employee lists and wage books on Form NOSI 2 for founders and staff, and register the payroll plan. Obtain social insurance numbers necessary for payroll and annual tax filings.
required_dossiers: Board resolution appointing the employer representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NOSI defers due to incomplete wage data, resubmit corrected payroll schedules; disputes can be submitted to the Pension Grievance Committee under Social Insurance Law No. 79 of 1975.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) is not applicable for ISIC 6201 information technology; the operative licensors for the physical workplace are the Local District (Hayy/City Council) for the municipal business license and the Civil Defense Authority for occupancy safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Activity License (Rukhsah Tijariyah) and Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate for Professional Office

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) - Law No. 4 of 1994
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D - Exempt / Non-polluting office information service; no EIA report required; only general sanitary sewage and waste segregation obligations apply
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater, no VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste. Domestic wastewater must meet Law No. 93 of 1962 public sewer standards; electronic equipment waste, when generated, must be handed to a licensed EEAA-approved e-waste recycler under the provisions of Law No. 4 of 1994.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance is mandatory and issued by the Civil Defense Authority after inspection of extinguishers, emergency exits, and electrical installations. Structural load compliance is reviewed against the Egyptian Building Code. Occupational safety and health documentation is assessed under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 and its executive regulations, covering first aid, signage, emergency lighting, and worker health records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Egyptian Ministry of Finance. Main portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing portal: https://einvoice.invoicing.eta.gov.eg; e-receipt portal: https://ereceipt.invoicing.eta.gov.eg. Unified national tax administration; no sub-national entity-level tax authorities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: incorporate the LLC at the Commercial Registry (Ministry of Trade and Industry) to obtain the Commercial Registration (CR) number and certificate of incorporation. Step 2: file the ETA Tax Card Application (Form 1) with the competent district tax office, attaching the CR extract, authenticated memorandum/articles of association, board resolution, lease agreement, copies of manager/shareholder IDs, and bank confirmation; the ETA issues the unified tax card containing the 14-digit Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration references. Step 3: register for VAT on the same ETA file once annual taxable turnover reaches or is projected to reach EGP 500,000 (mandatory within 30 days); voluntary registration is allowed below the threshold and is advisable for export-oriented businesses to recover input VAT. Step 4: enroll in the ETA e-invoicing system by obtaining an ETA-accredited digital-signature certificate, completing portal onboarding, and activating production API credentials. Step 5: complete Social Insurance Authority (SISI) registration for payroll and open the foreign-currency account with an Egyptian authorized dealer bank for export proceeds. A foreign-owned LLC must maintain a resident tax representative/manager for ETA correspondence; non-resident pure digital service providers without an Egyptian establishment may instead use the ETA simplified foreign e-services registration procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: an Egyptian LLC is a juridical tax resident under Income Tax Law 91/2005 and is subject to corporate income tax at 22.5% on worldwide net income. No pass-through or check-the-box classification is available; the LLC is taxed at entity level, and profit distributions are subject to 10% dividend withholding. Treaty and unilateral foreign-tax-credit relief may apply to foreign-source income, but no general territorial exemption exists. The software/fintech services profile does not change the statutory classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not recognize US-style check-the-box elections; classification follows statutory corporate form. Available elections: (a) Law 20/2020 SME presumptive-tax regime for annual turnover up to EGP 20 million, with final revenue-based cash-basis rates of 0.5%, 0.75%, 1% and 1.5% by turnover bracket, elected by formal ETA notification before the first return; (b) depreciation and inventory valuation method elections declared in the first CIT return; (c) voluntary early VAT registration before crossing the EGP 500,000 threshold; (d) advance pricing agreements (APA) with the ETA transfer-pricing unit for cross-border service contracts; and (e) treaty-based withholding-rate reductions claimed through ETA double-tax relief forms. No fiscal-unity (tax grouping) election and no hybrid-mismatch unilateral election exist under Egyptian domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016 and Executive Regulation No. 1205 of 2016, as amended by subsequent ETA decrees through 2025, including the electronic invoicing framework, the reverse-charge mechanism for imported services, and the non-resident digital-supplier registration regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 per annum of taxable turnover; mandatory registration within 30 days of crossing the threshold (Article 28 of VAT Law 67/2016). Registration is also required without threshold for goods importers and for entities seeking input-VAT recovery on exports. Non-resident suppliers of digital services to Egyptian consumers are required to register through the ETA foreign-supplier e-portal regardless of the EGP 500,000 threshold; services imported from non-residents by Egyptian businesses remain subject to reverse-charge withholding at 14%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory. Since the phased introduction beginning 15 November 2020, all ETA-registered enterprises are progressively required to submit e-invoices (B2B/B2G) and, under the e-receipt program, B2C retail receipts in real time. Documents are transmitted in XML (UBL 2.1) or JSON to the ETA e-invoicing API (Rased central platform), which performs XSD schema validation, XAdES digital-signature verification, TIN/CR cross-checks, and business-rule validation. Upon clearance the ETA returns a unique digital stamp code (UUID and QR block) that must be embedded in the invoice; a document that fails validation or lacks the stamp is treated as never issued and cannot support input-VAT deduction. API integration uses OAuth 2.0 client-credentials authentication with HMAC-signed payloads and an active on-boarded digital certificate. Non-compliance creates a presumption of undeclared revenue and may result in risk-engine blacklisting and business suspension orders.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating is available for (a) tangible goods physically exported through Egyptian customs, and (b) services supplied by an Egyptian VAT-registered supplier to a non-resident recipient where the benefit is wholly consumed abroad, including software-as-a-service, cloud infrastructure, and financial portfolio tracking applications. The exporter must evidence the non-resident status of the recipient (overseas tax/CR certificate), maintain a written export contract addressed abroad, issue a foreign-currency commercial invoice, and channel proceeds through an Egyptian authorized dealer bank. For app-store based software exports (Stripe and Apple IAP rails), platform payout statements, end-user IP/geolocation evidence, and overseas subscriber contracts are accepted as supplementary proof that the service is consumed outside Egypt. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is refundable under Article 23 of VAT Law 67/2016.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through the Egyptian Single Window (NAFEZA) identifying the exporter as legal owner and specifying the HS code and physical exit record
Export contract and commercial invoice showing FOB/CIF value, foreign-currency payment terms, and recipient address outside Egypt
Original Bill of Lading (ocean), Air Waybill (air), or CMR/road manifest naming the Egyptian exporter as consignor/shipper
Packing list and container/seal or terminal exit receipt evidencing departure from Egyptian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank credit advice from the Egyptian authorized dealer confirming foreign-currency receipt and conversion within the CBE repatriation window
VAT return e-file schedule of zero-rated export supplies together with the cleared e-invoice marked with the export indicator
For digital services: platform payout statements (Stripe/Apple IAP), IP-geolocation data of end users, and the overseas subscriber contract
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA reconciles the zero-rated export schedule against NAFEZA customs exit data, CBE foreign-exchange records, and bank IRCs. Failure to substantiate the export within the 180-day repatriation window triggers immediate reassessment at 14% VAT, a monthly 2% late-payment addition (Article 30 of VAT Law 67/2016), and complete clawback of any input VAT previously refunded. Where export documents are falsified or transactions are circular/reversed, Article 66 imposes fines of up to EGP 2,000,000 and imprisonment, extends the five-year assessment period, and the CBE may block the exporter's commercial registration and trade-finance facilities. The Law 4/2023 tax-penalty reconciliation facility permits early settlement of late additions at reduced rates but does not extinguish criminal liability for forged export evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole monetary, banking-licensing, and foreign-exchange authority; the Ministry of Finance and General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) govern entity registration, while the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) administers tax-clearance gates for capital and profit remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The EGP operates under a managed floating exchange-rate regime following the March 2024 national FX unification. Current-account transactions, including cross-border software-service receipts, are freely convertible, and registered profit/dividend repatriation is permissible after ETA issuance of a tax-clearance certificate and completion of annual statutory audit. Capital-account items — equity injections, shareholder-loan conversions, and money-market investments — remain subject to CBE balance-of-payments reporting and bank-level compliance checks. Practical hurdles include interbank USD liquidity volatility, mandatory inward-declaration forms for foreign investment, and CBE scrutiny of whether the underlying revenue represents genuine Egyptian service exports rather than passive investment income.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE Circular 31 (as amended through the 2016 float and 2024 unification), exporters of goods and intangible services must repatriate export proceeds into an Egyptian bank account within 90 days from the contractual export/settlement date (180 days for permitted categories). For a fintech software exporter in ISIC 6201, the shipment-evidence trigger is the signed SaaS/subscription contract and e-invoice rather than customs declarations. There is no mandatory conversion ratio today — exporters may retain USD proceeds in foreign-currency accounts or sell them voluntarily at the interbank rate. Failure to repatriate within the statutory timeline exposes the exporter to suspension of its CBE export file, denial of FX trade facilities, and bank-imposed documentary penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EGP/USD current account and segregated USD capital-escalation ledger for the subscribed share-capital escrow
EGP operational account with associated USD current account and export-proceeds collection ledger
USD/EGP multi-currency operational account plus treasury-line booking account for FX-forward and swap execution
Multi-currency operational account (USD/EUR/EGP) optimised for cross-border vendor payments and SWIFT MT103 throughput
Operational account with trade-settlement desk and import-LC booking window

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: VIABILITY RATING: LOW as a full banking substitute; LIMITED SAFE-HARBOR as a collection-only intermediary. CBE Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 requires any entity that handles EGP payments, issues payment instruments, or provides payment-account services to Egyptian residents to hold a CBE-issued license. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business, etc.) hold no Egyptian banking or PSP license and therefore cannot maintain EGP settlement accounts, receive interbank EGP transfers, or function as a primary clearing rail. Their permissible role is confined to collecting USD proceeds from merchant-of-record rails (Stripe, Apple IAP) and executing an onward SWIFT MT103 credit to the EG_LLC USD account at a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank, with full UBO and sanctions reporting completed through the receiving bank's KYC channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: DIRECTORS MUST APPEAR PHYSICALLY. Egyptian anti-money-laundering instructions under CBE regulations and the Egyptian AML Law require at least two authorised signatories — including the managing director — to appear in person before the compliance officer at a CBE-licensed branch in Egypt. Fully remote video onboarding is not accepted for a newly incorporated LLC with 100% non-resident shareholders. The physical interview is mandatory for signature verification, source-of-funds discussion, and UBO attestation swearing. Original passports, certified constitutional documents, and the GAFI investment certificate must be presented at the Cairo or Alexandria branch; attestation through overseas embassies is permitted for documents but does not waive the in-person appointment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: 100% shareholding held by a UAE-based intellectual-property and holding vehicle, creating concern over the ultimate natural-person beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised UBO declaration mapping all natural persons above 5%; certified corporate register excerpt of the UAE parent; passport copies of all direct and indirect shareholders; UAE Economic Substance / Commercial License certificate; GAFI registration certificate; Egyptian Commercial Registry extract; audited parent financial statements for the last 24 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fintech keyword risk: the description 'financial portfolio tracking' triggers bank suspicion that the entity requires a CBE PSP licence or engages in unauthorised fund custody.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written legal opinion from Egyptian counsel confirming that the SaaS product is a data-analytics and wealth-visualisation application, outside the licensing scope of CBE Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 and the Financial Regulatory Authority's fintech licensing list; a product functional-flow document proving the company never takes possession of client funds; the merchant-of-record agreement with Apple/Stripe; ISIC 6201 business-scope certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds insufficiency and incomplete capital-injection trail for the USD share capital contribution from the UAE parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12 months of UAE-parent bank statements; notarised board resolution approving the EG_LLC capital contribution; shareholder-sworn source-of-wealth statement; UAE corporate tax/filing acknowledgements showing legitimate earnings; Egyptian statutory-auditor capital-attestation letter; GAFI capital-amendment filing receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Treaty/tax-avoidance red flag: perceived diversion of profits from Egypt to a zero-rate UAE free-zone vehicle at artificially pegged service fees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic-Substance (UAE free-zone) certificate; complete transfer-pricing documentation benchmarking the SaaS analytics licence fee on an OECD-aligned basis; Egyptian e-invoice records and ETA tax-card; headcount and payroll substance evidence for EG_LLC; the Egypt-UAE tax treaty residence certificate for the parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions- and PEP-screening concerns on non-resident directors and the UAE holding vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-grade sanctions-screening results against UN, OFAC, EU, and CBE Circular 105 lists for all shareholders and signatories; UAE authority court-record and warrant clearances; verified business-address documentation (utility bills and tenancy contracts); signed political-exposure declarations for each beneficial owner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) the UAE parent bank executes a SWIFT MT103 wire to the EG_LLC USD account at a CBE-licensed bank with remitter designated as 'direct investor' and narration 'EG_LLC - equity capital contribution'; (2) the receiving bank maps the credit to the CBE balance-of-payments reporting template under 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital Injection', using the purpose code indicated in the bank's inward-remittance questionnaire rather than generic 'personal remittance'; (3) funds are posted to a restricted 'capital escrow' ledger and are not convertible to EGP until the statutory auditor issues a capital-attestation certificate and the company completes the GAFI/Commercial-Registry capital-amendment filing; (4) upon ETA tax-card presentation and the auditor's release voucher, the bank transfers funds to the operating USD account or converts them at the prevailing interbank rate; (5) any bank commissions, FX spreads, and VAT on banking services are booked on separately itemised invoices to preserve deductibility.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Service imports (cloud hosting, SaaS licensing, subcontractors, legal and accounting fees) are cleared via SWIFT MT103 transfers from the Egyptian bank, supported by the underlying invoice, service contract, and the applicable withholding-tax statement on royalties/services (20% domestic rate, reduced under the Egypt-UAE tax treaty where eligible). Physical-goods imports are cleared via commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) where the vendor requires documentary protection or the transaction value exceeds the bank's open-account threshold; the CBE imposes no mandatory LC requirement in the current regime, but the bank's electronic payment order and customs-form linkage must show a valid import purpose code. Cross-border subscription revenue collected through Apple IAP and Stripe must be swept via SWIFT MT103 to the EG_LLC USD operating account, after which the bank registers the inflow in the CBE export database with the narrative 'digital service exports - ISIC 6201', thereby preserving the export-proceeds timeline for the 90-day repatriation rule.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP FX forward contracts with a CBE-licensed counterparty, executed against documented real trade/investment exposure (permitted without CBE pre-approval for current-account hedging).
Offshore USD/EGP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) arranged through an international bank arm, settling in USD outside Egypt while the EGP leg stays non-deliverable offshore.
USD/EGP cross-currency swaps for long-dated balance-sheet hedging of equity capital and retained earnings, requiring bank treasury approval and CBE transaction tagging.

Natural hedging through matched USD subscription receivables and USD cloud/vendor payables, supplemented by holding USD treasury balances in the Egyptian operating account to reduce periodic conversion frequency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (CIT) for companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year LLC, no later than 30 April of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge, interest on unpaid tax, and ETA enforcement measures, including bank account seizure; failure to file the CIT return may prevent issuance of the tax clearance certificate needed for commercial registry transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements with the independent auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Commercial Registry e-filing and ETA as tax-file attachment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be finalized and audited within six months after the fiscal year-end; the GAFI filing of the adopted statements occurs within ten days after approval by the general assembly.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: GAFI warning, suspension of commercial-register certification, and administrative strike-off proceedings for repeated failure; managers and the external auditor remain civilly liable for inaccurate statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general assembly meeting, AGM minutes, and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI when the AGM approves amendments to the memorandum or quota transfers; statutory registers retained on-site
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened within six months after the fiscal year-end; any register-affecting resolution or quota transfer amendment must be submitted to GAFI within fifteen days of the qualifying event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM or maintain minutes exposes managers to GAFI regulatory warning, personal liability for damages, and, in recurrent non-compliance, an administrative dissolution procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll and social insurance reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority and National Social Insurance Authority (NSSA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly declarations and payment deposits are due monthly; the annual employee withholding-tax return is reconciled and submitted no later than 31 March of the following calendar year for the prior fiscal year payroll.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment penalties, NSSA administrative fines, interest on due contributions, and listing of the company as a delinquent employer; willful non-remittance may be prosecuted as tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial registry and tax-card annual verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI Commercial Registry and the competent governorate licensing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal and verification are performed during the first quarter of each operating year; any change to the registered address, managers, or shareholding structure is filed with GAFI within fifteen days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of the commercial register record and tax card; fines under the Commercial Registration Law; the company loses the ability to open bank accounts, invoice public-sector clients, or clear goods through customs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register annual review and update confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained on-site and made available to GAFI and the Egyptian AML Unit on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Updated immediately upon any direct or indirect ownership change and formally reviewed no later than the AGM date within six months after the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML-law administrative penalties for inaccurate or stale UBO data, including fines and possible restriction of bank relationships, enforceable by GAFI in coordination with the Egyptian AML Unit.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory for all Egyptian LLCs: Companies Law 159/1981 requires at least one auditor registered with the Egyptian Federation of Accountants and Auditors to audit the annual financial statements; no revenue-based exemption applies while the LLC is active.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS, as adopted by the Ministry of Finance; consolidated and standalone statutory accounts are prepared under EAS for tax and GAFI filing purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The AGM confirms the updated register of members annually. Quota transfers are valid only upon notarization, entry in the register of members, and amendment of the GAFI commercial-register record; the beneficial ownership register is refreshed on any direct or indirect ownership change and reviewed each AGM cycle. Egypt does not require a separate free-standing UBO return for a standard LLC absent an AML information request or approval event, but records must be available for inspection.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $500–$1,500 per year for registered office and corporate secretarial agent services in Cairo or Giza
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,500–$4,500 per year for a standard fintech LLC with simplified EAS statements and one revenue stream

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% corporate income tax (CIT) on taxable commercial profits of the EG_LLC under Law No. 91 of 2005 (Income Tax Law), as amended by Law No. 2 of 2018 and subsequent finance laws.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday applies to the fintech LLC. Preferential treatment is limited to qualifying strategic or golden-license projects under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (investment-cost deduction of 30%–50% in designated governorates/economic zones), SCZone-approved platform projects (0%–10% CIT for committed developers), and ordinary deductions for traceable software development/R&D expenditures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 19 (Juristic Persons Income Tax Return) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) unified e-filing portal (e-Taamal / eta.gov.eg), linked to the taxpayer tax card; audited financial statements and the transfer-pricing disclosure annex are uploaded as attachments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 4 months after the fiscal year-end (the EG_LLC closes books on 31 December unless a different accounting year was pre-approved by the ETA); the return is a self-assessment and the tax payable must be settled at or before the filing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Identification (Tax Card No., CR No., fiscal year start/end)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registers the LLC's Egyptian tax card number, commercial registry number, and exact accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must state the legal representative and financial controller resident in Egypt; a foreign manager files under a notarised power of attorney stamped with foreign legalisation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Gross revenue (international subscription and analytics fees)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide gross receipts booked by the LLC from financial portfolio tracking, including Stripe and Apple IAP proceeds, adjusted to Egyptian GAAP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Egypt-attributable revenue is taxable; apportionment must follow the arm's-length rules and cannot be reduced by the foreign parent's group rebates absent substantiation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 and 9 – Deductible vs. non-deductible expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating costs supported by e-invoices, depreciation, and amortisation of product development; clearly separated from personal, non-business, or penalty expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border intercompany charges (cloud hosting, licensing, software maintenance) are deductible only if a valid invoice, contract, TP documentation, and WHT certificate for royalties/fees exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offsets taxable income with carried-forward losses of the preceding 5 years (original-year losses only, no change-of-control limitation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss schedule is available for inspection by the ETA inspector; a non-resident review should verify that the 5-year limitation is tracked per statutory year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate value of controlled transactions with foreign parent, affiliates, and connected directors; triggers the TP compliance requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the aggregate amount exceeds EGP 2 million, the TP disclosure annex and, above EGP 10 million, Local/Master Files must be uploaded; the non-resident group must appoint an Egyptian TP coordinator.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed net taxable income after statutory add-backs, deductions, and loss carryforward; CIT calculated at the headline 22.5% rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any double-tax treaty adjustments and foreign tax credits are treated as post-calculation credits, not as income deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 24 – Advance tax payments and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for quarterly advance CIT payments and withholding tax suffered on Egyptian-sourced interest/royalty income, plus foreign tax credits under the applicable DTA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign tax credit is allowed only to the extent of Egyptian tax on the same income and only with an official foreign tax receipt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 29 – Net tax payable / refund claimed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance due to the ETA treasury or refundable excess; payment instruction and e-signature of the legal representative complete the filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds are routed to an Egyptian bank account of the LLC; no refund will be processed until the annual TP filing and e-invoice status are cleared.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a monthly delay fine of 2% of the unpaid tax per month or part thereof (capped at 50% of the assessed tax), plus late-payment interest at 0.75% per month on the balance; when no tax is due, an administrative fine of EGP 500–EGP 5,000 applies; intentional non-filing or fraudulent concealment is referred to the Economic Courts as tax evasion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annex TP-1 (Transfer Pricing Disclosure Annex) and e-invoice/e-receipt reconciliation file, filed simultaneously with Form No. 19 on the ETA portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same statutory 4-month deadline as Form No. 19; the annex must cover all controlled transactions of the closed fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Table A – Controlled transactions by category
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenues, costs, royalties, management fees, and interest with related parties, segregated by counterparty and country.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian LLC reports the gross amounts payable to/receivable from each foreign affiliate and confirms the arm's-length treatment method used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Table B – Intercompany pricing method applied
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, or profit split consistent with the Egyptian TP Guidelines.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A benchmark study must substantiate the chosen method for the non-resident-controlled relationship; ETA may impute a default price if no study is uploaded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Headcount, key functions, risk control, contracts, and book flows for the Egyptian entity and each related party.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Shell or pass-through descriptions are fatal: ETA re-characterises the non-resident controller as a permanent establishment of the Egyptian LLC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to upload Annex TP-1: administrative fine of EGP 40,000–EGP 100,000, mandatory TP adjustment, and loss of the burden of proof; the ETA can impose a 2% monthly delay fine on any resulting under-assessed tax, capped at 50%.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax (WHT) on gross dividends distributed by the Egyptian LLC to non-resident shareholders under Article 56 of Law No. 91 of 2005; distributions to resident corporate shareholders holding 25% or more may claim the domestic participation exemption, but distributions to foreign portfolio shareholders remain subject to 10% unless a treaty reduces the rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder obtains a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the treaty-country tax authority (apostilled/legalised, showing beneficial ownership), completes the ETA DTA relief declaration (national forms DTA-1/DTA-2 in practice), and delivers them to the Egyptian withholding agent before the distribution so that the reduced treaty rate (commonly 5%–15% by holding percentage) is applied at source; ETA approval is confirmed via the e-filing portal. Where excess WHT was already deducted, the recipient files a refund claim within 5 years, supported by the TRC, distribution minutes, and WHT certificates, or triggers the mutual agreement procedure of the applicable double-tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 20% for royalties/technical licence fees paid for the use of the portfolio-tracking software, patents, algorithms, and know-how, and 20% for interest on intercompany loans, bonds, or deposits paid to non-resident lenders; a 10% WHT applies to dividends and profit distributions. Under most of Egypt's comprehensive DTAs (including China, the UK, the Netherlands, Germany, and Turkey), interest and royalties may be reduced to 0%–15% and dividends to 5%–15%, contingent on beneficial ownership and treaty limits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10 million of aggregate controlled transactions per fiscal year triggers preparation of the Local File and Master File; an Annex TP-1 disclosure in Form 19 is mandatory once controlled transactions exceed EGP 2 million; Country-by-Country Reporting applies where the ultimate parent's consolidated group revenue reaches EGP 3 billion.
